findings.title: A link named EXPORT-NOTE.txt in the project's history makes the export overwrite a file outside its temporary folder, the acceptance store included
findings.file_line: builder/src/orchestrator/export.ts:111-120 (the write); :81-82 (the only check on names, which covers acceptance/ only)
findings.what: After the clone, the export writes its note with writeFileSync at <copy>/EXPORT-NOTE.txt. If the last commit of the workspace history holds a symbolic link of that name, git checks the link out and Node writes through it. The builder runs as root (gaps 57, 135), so whatever the link names is overwritten, or created, with the note's text (fixed text, so this destroys or creates files; it does not let the author choose the content). The export still finishes and is recorded with label and acceptance_in_exported_copy_only: true, yet the exported copy carries no 'Internal only, not for customers' note: its EXPORT-NOTE.txt is the link, and the export's own commit does not contain the note. NOT reachable today: only the template copy and the scripted steps' exact fixed files are ever committed (scripted.ts:334-353 fails a step whose changes are not exactly the manifest's plain files), and none is a link. It becomes reachable with any engine that may write files of its own choosing.
findings.scenario: RAN (p1-note-symlink.ts, p12-store-reach.ts; from wtrev14/builder: node --import tsx <probe>). Commit, with commitAll, a link EXPORT-NOTE.txt pointing at: (a) an existing file outside every export folder: after writeExport that file reads "Internal only, not for customers. ...", export ok, the copy's EXPORT-NOTE.txt is a link, the export commit lists only the three acceptance files; (b) ../../../../../../created-by-export.txt: a new file appears outside the staging folder; (c) ../../../../../acceptance/<project id>/v001/manifest.json, which needs no knowledge of the machine's folders (five levels up from the copy is the data folder): the export succeeds, then the store's manifest of the version fixed at plan confirmation holds the note's text, verifyVersion fails ("the manifest cannot be read"), and a second export is refused. Control: a link named acceptance is refused by the existing check. Read, not run: the same link could name the interface's password digest file in the data folder (auth.ts then refuses to start), a file of the workspace, or a device.
findings.known_gap: None records it. Nearest is gap 51 (files the engine writes acting on git on the host; 'used with the scripted engine only; package 2.2 must not rely on it'), but this is the export's own write, not git's.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not write through the checked-out tree. After the clone, lstat <copy>/EXPORT-NOTE.txt and <copy>/acceptance and refuse if anything at all is there (do not rely on git's list of names); create each file exclusively without following a link (open with O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW). Stronger: make the export's commit with git plumbing (hash-object -w --no-filters, update-index --add --cacheinfo, commit) and let git check it out, so Node never writes into a tree the engine authored. Add a test with a link at that name, shown failing without the safeguard.

findings.title: A .gitignore or .gitattributes in the project's history keeps the tests out of the export's commit, or changes their bytes on checkout, and the export still reports success
findings.file_line: builder/src/orchestrator/export.ts:121-125 (plain git add, commit, no check of what was committed); builder/src/orchestrator/journey-jobs.ts:588-599 (the event's literal acceptance_in_exported_copy_only: true)
findings.what: The acceptance folder is added with a plain `git add -- acceptance EXPORT-NOTE.txt` inside the cloned copy, where the project's own .gitignore and .gitattributes apply. .gitignore is not a protected path (scripted.ts:50-64). git skips ignored files inside a named folder silently, and nothing afterwards checks that the commit holds the manifest's files with the manifest's fingerprints. Design note 2.7 says the exporter 'copies ... into acceptance/ in the exported repository and commits it there'; here the files can be present in the archive only as untracked, ignored files, while the record says the tests are in the exported copy. NOT reachable today: the template's .gitignore (node_modules/, .next/, .env, certs/*.crt, licences.csv) matches none of these files, there is no attributes file, and the scripted steps cannot change either.
findings.scenario: RAN (p3-ignore-attrs.ts). A commit that changes .gitignore, then writeExport: `*.spec.ts` -> export ok, the export's commit holds only EXPORT-NOTE.txt, acceptance/README.txt, acceptance/v001/manifest.json; `/acceptance/v*/` -> README and note only; `/acceptance/*` -> the note only; `manifest.json` -> no manifest in the commit. In each case `git status --ignored` in the copy shows the test as ignored and a clone of the exported repository has no tests. `.gitattributes` with `acceptance/** text eol=crlf` -> the committed blob matches the manifest, but a fresh clone of the exported copy checks item-01.spec.ts out with CRLF line ends, SHA-256 b5e12fbe... against the manifest's 95b2b71f.... Cases that fail closed (export refused): `/acceptance` or `EXPORT-NOTE.txt` ignored whole (git add errors), and `working-tree-encoding=UTF-16LE` on the tests.
findings.known_gap: None. Gap 51 names .gitattributes only for the question of git running a program on the host.
findings.suggested_fix: Add with `git add -f`, then verify from the commit itself before the archive is made: `git ls-tree -r HEAD -- acceptance EXPORT-NOTE.txt` is exactly the expected list, each a plain file, and each blob's SHA-256 (git cat-file blob) equals the manifest's; refuse otherwise. Refuse when `git check-ignore` or `git check-attr -a` reports anything for those paths in the cloned tree (a later checkout by the receiver obeys the in-tree attributes). Or commit by plumbing with --no-filters. Record the verified fingerprints in journey.export.written instead of a literal true. Tests for each, with controls.

findings.title: The refusals for an acceptance folder and for secret-looking files read git's quoted names, so unusual names pass; names that differ only by letter case pass too
findings.file_line: builder/src/orchestrator/export.ts:81-84 (names read without -z, compared as text); :45-47 (secretLikePath)
findings.what: The names come from `git log --name-only` split on newlines. git wraps any name holding a double quote, a backslash, a tab or another control character in quotes with escapes (core.quotePath=false only stops the quoting of non-ASCII bytes). A quoted name starts with a quote character and ends with one, so `f.startsWith("acceptance/")` and the `$`-anchored secret patterns do not match it. Both checks are also case-sensitive. So the header's statement 'The export is refused if any commit of the history holds ... an acceptance folder' does not hold for such names, and the exported acceptance folder can hold files the engine wrote next to the store's, under a README that says the folder was copied from the store and that the project's history does not hold these files. NOT reachable today (no such names in the template or the fixed change sets; checked with find).
findings.scenario: RAN (p2-quoted.ts, p12-store-reach.ts P13). History with acceptance/v001/item-9"9.spec.ts, acceptance/v001/helper<TAB>.ts and acceptance/back\slash.txt: the check reads "\"acceptance/v001/item-9\\\"9.spec.ts\"" and so on, export ok, and the exported acceptance/v001 holds helper<TAB>.ts, item-01.spec.ts, item-9"9.spec.ts, manifest.json: two files a test runner's *.spec.ts pattern would match, one of them the engine's. keys/server"1.pem and keys/tab<TAB>.key are exported; secretLikePath gives true on the raw names and false on git's quoted form. History with Acceptance/v001/item-01.spec.ts, Acceptance/v001/manifest.json and export-note.txt: export ok, the archive holds both spellings (entry order: EXPORT-NOTE.txt, export-note.txt, acceptance/..., Acceptance/...). READ only, not run (no such file system here): on a case-insensitive file system (macOS, Windows) the two spellings are one folder and one file, so the later archive entry, here the engine's, replaces the builder's on unpacking.
findings.known_gap: None. Gap 51 lists 'an unusual file name' among things not shown for git on the host; it does not cover these two refusals.
findings.suggested_fix: Read names with `-z` and split on NUL (git never quotes then). Compare the first path component after lower-casing and Unicode normalisation, and after trimming trailing dots and spaces, against `acceptance` and `export-note.txt`; apply secretLikePath case-insensitively to the raw names. Keep the lstat check of finding 1 after the clone as the check that does not depend on names. Tests for a quoted name, a case variant and a secret-looking quoted name, each shown failing without the fix.

findings.title: The export does not compare the store's version with what was recorded when the plan was confirmed, and it copies after checking
findings.file_line: builder/src/orchestrator/export.ts:75-76 (verifyVersion only) and :98 (copy by path, later); builder/src/orchestrator/journey-jobs.ts:585-587 (no database handed to writeExport); compare builder/src/acceptance/runner.ts:98-108 and :119-124; builder/src/acceptance/store.ts:112-115 and :279-284
findings.what: Three related gaps on the store side. (a) writeExport checks the version only against its own manifest. The runner also compares the manifest's fingerprint and items with the builder's acceptance.version.written event (versionMatchesEvent) and refuses on a difference; the export has no such comparison and is not given the database, and journey.export.written does not record the manifest's fingerprint. (b) The check reads and hashes the files; the copy is made later by path with copyFileSync, which follows links, after the workspace's `git log` and the clone; nothing hashes the copies. (c) verifyVersion lstat's only the version folder, so the project's folder in the store may be a link. All three need write access to the data folder on the host. No container has it: the store is mounted read-only, in the runner only (runner.ts:158), and the engine mount rule refuses it. So neither the engine nor the app can do this as designed; finding 1 reaches the store but writes only fixed text.
findings.scenario: RAN (p5-store.ts). P5: replace item-01.spec.ts with another test and rewrite manifest.json to name its new fingerprint: verifyVersion ok, the manifest's SHA-256 differs from the one written at confirmation (8659f6fd... against eaac73e4...), writeExport ok, and the exported, committed test is the forged one; the runner would refuse this same store (read: runner.ts:102). P8: swap item-01.spec.ts for a link to another file on the host immediately after writeExport's check (the check is synchronous at the top; the swap is done before its first git command returns): export ok, and the exported, committed item-01.spec.ts is a plain file holding that other file's content. P6a: the project's folder in the store replaced by a link to a copy elsewhere: verifyVersion ok, export ok. Controls that were refused: a link in place of a test file; a link in place of the version folder; manifest file names '../../../../../etc/hostname', '/etc/hostname', 'sub/item-01.spec.ts', 'item-01.spec.ts/' and one with a NUL byte.
findings.known_gap: Gap 71 covers the class (a version is protected by the builder's own code only; the check is a moment, not a lock) but states that 'the manifest is compared with its acceptance.version.written event': true of the runner, not of the export.
findings.suggested_fix: Give writeExport the database (or the recorded fingerprint and items) and call versionMatchesEvent as the runner does. After copying, hash each copy in the staging folder (opened without following a link) against the manifest, and the manifest copy against the recorded fingerprint, before the commit. lstat the project's folder in the store as well as the version folder. Put manifest_sha256 into journey.export.written. Tests: a version replaced whole is refused; a file swapped between check and copy is refused.

findings.title: The archive names this machine's sandbox folder, though the code says the copy does not point back at it
findings.what: `git remote remove origin` removes the remote, but the clone's reference log stays in the archive and records where it was cloned from.
findings.scenario: RAN (p9-misc.ts). After a plain export, grep of the unpacked copy for the sandbox path finds .git/logs/HEAD and .git/logs/refs/heads/main; the first line ends 'clone: from <sandbox>/workspace.git'. Nothing else in the copy names it (no remote, no alternates file; .git/config holds only the four core lines).
findings.known_gap: None.
findings.suggested_fix: Clone with `-c core.logAllRefUpdates=false`, or remove .git/logs before the archive is made; add to the export test a search of the unpacked copy for the sandbox folder's path.

findings.title: The secret check is by file name only, case-sensitive, and its list is short; this limit is not recorded
findings.what: secretLikePath knows .env files, five key and certificate endings, a secrets/ folder and three id_ names. It never reads content. The header calls it 'a file that looks like a secret', which is honest, but KNOWN-GAPS has no entry saying the export's check is by name and what it misses. Today the engine's container holds none of the builder's secrets, so a miss needs the engine to have a secret in the first place.
findings.scenario: RAN (direct calls in p2-quoted.ts): false for .npmrc, .netrc, .pgpass, id_dsa, .ENV, credentials.json, service-account.json, .aws/credentials, x.jks, x.keystore, secret/token.
findings.known_gap: None found (searched KNOWN-GAPS for 'export', 'secret', 'by name').
findings.suggested_fix: Record the limit as a known gap. Fold case, and widen the list (.npmrc, .netrc, .pgpass, id_dsa, *.jks, *.keystore, credentials*, service-account*).

findings.title: Archive handling: the earlier archive is removed before the new one exists, and there is no size limit before the export is recorded
findings.what: (a) rmSync removes <project>-export.tar.gz before tar runs; if tar, chmod or the hashing then fails, the earlier export's event names a file that is gone and its download answers 'not found'. (b) The whole archive is read into memory to hash it. A history holding large files that do not compress (which an engine free to write files could make) gives an archive over 200 MB that is recorded as written but that the file route never serves (maxBytes), and over 2 GiB readFileSync throws after the archive is written, leaving it on disk with no record (the finally block removes only the staging folder).
findings.scenario: READ only; not run (large files not tried).
findings.known_gap: None.
findings.suggested_fix: Write the archive under a temporary name and rename it into place only after it is hashed; hash by stream; refuse, before recording, an archive larger than the route serves; remove a failed archive.

tried_and_held: (5) Export for a project not signed off, or a broken copy: read JOB_RULES.export (journey.ts:551) and startJob (stopped, closed and interrupted projects refused; rule checked under the project's lock); writeExport has one caller (journey-jobs.ts:587) behind one route. Ran three existing tests under the shared lock, all passed: 'export is refused before sign-off, and allowed after it', 'A6: a broken copy whose run reads passed (a forged pass) ...', 'the export: a .tar.gz of the project's history ...'. I found no way round the rule.

(3) A program run during the export: p11b.ts planted, in a commit, .gitattributes naming filter, diff, merge and textconv drivers on every file and on acceptance/**, a .gitmodules with an ext:: address, a .lfsconfig, a workspace .gitconfig (fsmonitor, hooksPath, sshCommand, a filter with required=true, a diff driver), eight executable hook-named files, and (further than an engine can go) a gitlink made with plumbing. The canary file was never made through git log, clone, add or commit. With a gitlink plus `update = !command` in .gitmodules, git log itself stops ('invalid value for submodule.sub.update'), so the export is refused and nothing runs.

A planted .git folder in the working copy at export time (p14-planted-git.ts: settings naming fsmonitor, pager, hooksPath and packObjectsHook, plus hooks), with an uncommitted .env and an uncommitted acceptance/ file: no program ran; neither uncommitted file is in the archive; the exported acceptance/v001 holds only the store's two files.

(2) Writing back: the sandbox folder (workspace and workspace.git) was the same before and after a plain export, by path, mode, size, modification time and content (p9-misc.ts); the copy has no remote.
A link in the history to a file of the host (p10 in p9-misc.ts): the archive holds the link itself; the host file's content is not in the archive.
A link named `acceptance` in the history: refused by the existing check (p1-note-symlink.ts, control).

Manifest tricks: file names with ../, an absolute path, a sub-folder, a trailing slash, a NUL byte; a link in place of a test file; a link in place of the version folder: all refused by verifyVersion (p5-store.ts, controls).

Ignore and attribute cases that fail closed: `/acceptance` or `EXPORT-NOTE.txt` ignored as a whole, and working-tree-encoding=UTF-16LE on the tests: git add errors and the export is refused; `ident` and unknown filter names changed nothing.

The download route (read): an event of that project only, the file inside the project's exports folder with links resolved, opened without following a final link, size limit, gzip start bytes, the recorded SHA-256; the attachment name is cleaned.

Mounts (read): the engine service mounts the workspace, an empty folder over certs, and the change sets read-only (manager.ts:284-286); workspace.git is not mounted anywhere; the store version is mounted read-only in the runner only (runner.ts:158).

Reachability today (read, plus a find over templates/next and builder/scripted): the template and the two fixed change sets hold no link, no unusual or case-variant name, no .gitattributes or .gitmodules; a scripted step whose changes are not exactly its manifest's plain files fails before the commit. So findings 1 to 3 cannot be triggered in J1 as it runs today.
not_looked_at: The cameras' mounts (the other half of the adversarial reading J1's build brief asks for).
The export through the real interface with real containers (scripts/demo-journey.ts): the probes call writeExport directly, with commits made by the builder's own commitAll, and no Docker.

Whether a process in the engine container can learn the host's folder paths (for a link with an absolute target): inferred, not run. The store is reachable by a relative link without that (finding 1, case c).
Unpacking or checking out the export on a case-insensitive file system (finding 3's last step): not run.

Very large files (over 200 MB, over 2 GiB), folder trees deeper than the path limit (gap 58), and more than 20 MB of file names (git's output limit in export.ts:39 and project-repo.ts:74): read only; each appears to fail closed.

Whether the app that was accepted was built from exactly the committed tree: the preview job (journey-jobs.ts:444-478) does not compare the working copy with the last commit before the image build; buildAndStart was not read in full. Outside this area.

Noticed, not a tampering matter: writeExport throws plain errors, so a refused export shows the owner only 'the job stopped with an error (Error)' (journey.ts:1143); the real reason goes to the fault log.
Package 3.2's exporter, and git versions other than 2.43.0.
Running note for whoever repeats the probes: `npx tsx <file>` fails under this scratchpad because tsx's socket path is too long; `node --import tsx <file>` from wtrev14/builder works.
review.verdict: Nothing blocking: no hard rule is broken and J1's "Done means" stands, because today only the template and the scripted engine's exact fixed files reach a project's history and no container can write the store. Four serious weaknesses, each shown by a run, would let a hostile engine's files (a link named EXPORT-NOTE.txt, an ignore or attributes file, unusual or case-variant names) or a changed store overwrite files outside the export's folder (the acceptance store's manifest included) and drop, add to or replace the exported tests while the export reports success; none is in KNOWN-GAPS, and they should be fixed and tested before any engine other than the scripted one, and before package 3.2 relies on the export.

challenge.reasoning:
I could not refute it. My own probe reproduced every claim that the first reviewer ran, and the code reading supports the rest.

WHAT I RAN
Probe: <scratchpad>/rev14-chal-note/probe.mts, run from wtrev14/builder with `node --import tsx`, as uid 0. It is written separately from the first reviewer's harness. It uses the real `initProjectRepo`, `commitAll`, `openStore`, `writeVersion`, `verifyVersion` and `writeExport`, and takes the exports folder from the real `journeyFolder(dataDir, id, "exports")`, as journey-jobs.ts:587 does.

- Control, no such name in the history: export ok; the copy's EXPORT-NOTE.txt is a plain file whose first line is the label; the export commit lists EXPORT-NOTE.txt and the three acceptance files.
- Control, a plain file EXPORT-NOTE.txt ("Ready for customers.") committed by the "engine": export ok; it is overwritten with the builder's note and committed. So only a link gets through.
- Absolute link to an existing file outside the data folder and the sandbox: export ok; that file now reads "Internal only, not for customers. ..."; the copy's EXPORT-NOTE.txt is still the link; the export commit lists only the three acceptance files; `result.files` still names EXPORT-NOTE.txt.
- Relative link `../../../../../acceptance/<id>/v001/manifest.json`: with the real folder layout it resolves exactly to the store's manifest (mode 444, in a folder of mode 555, neither of which stops root). `verifyVersion` was ok before. The export succeeded, the manifest then began "Internal only, ...", `verifyVersion` failed ("the manifest cannot be read"), and a second export was refused.
- Dangling relative link: export ok, and a new file appeared in the data folder, outside the staging folder.

My scratch work folder was removed afterwards. `git status` in the worktree was clean before and after. I used no database, no Docker and no existing test.

WHAT I READ
- export.ts:111-120 is a plain `writeFileSync` into the checked-out tree. Lines 81-82 refuse only `acceptance` and `acceptance/...`.
- journey-jobs.ts:587-599 writes `journey.export.written` with `label: EXPORT_LABEL` and `acceptance_in_exported_copy_only: true` unconditionally once `writeExport` returns. So the record would claim the label for a copy that holds no note. I did not run this through the interface.
- No test covers a link at that name; test/journey.test.ts:691-708 covers the plain case only.
- auth.ts:121-133: a digest file overwritten with the note's text makes the next start refuse. This matches the finding's "read, not run" claim.
- The project already treats link-following writes as defects elsewhere (files.ts and auth.ts use O_NOFOLLOW and O_EXCL; results.ts; J2's test A4c). export.ts itself treats the history as untrusted (the acceptance and secret-name refusals). So this is a miss inside the file's own stated defence.

ATTEMPTS TO REFUTE THAT FAILED
- Reachable today? No, as the finding itself says. The only writers of a project's history are `initProjectRepo` (the template copy) and scripted.ts:358, which runs after the exact-manifest check at scripted.ts:334-353 (lstat `isFile` plus SHA-256). There is no link and no EXPORT-NOTE file in templates/, builder/scripted or builder/scripted-broken. That is why it is not blocking: no hard rule is broken as the code runs now, and every item of J1's "Done means" (journey-j1.md section 3; the table in evidence/2026-11-13-journey-j1/journey.md) is still shown. 3.1b's criteria are not touched.
- Already recorded? No. I searched KNOWN-GAPS.md, DECISIONS.md and docs/reviews for the export together with links, checkout and EXPORT-NOTE. The nearest gaps are listed in the known-gap field.
- Severity too high? I considered "minor" because it is unreachable today. I keep serious-non-blocking. Under the hostile-engine brief this is a write (overwrite or create) of any path on the machine, as root, by the builder's own host-side code. It needs only a committed link, which `entriesGitCannotSee` explicitly allows, and a real engine cannot be held to an exact manifest. It also yields an export without the "Internal only, not for customers" note while the record says it carries that label.

CORRECTIONS TO THE FINDING (none changes the verdict)
- Lines 83-84 are also a check on names (secret-like paths), so 81-82 is not "the only check on names".
- The effect on the acceptance store fails closed. The damaged version is caught by `verifyVersion`, so runs and exports are refused. This is destruction, not a forged pass, and the text is fixed.
- That the engine can learn the project id for the relative variant is not shown. The absolute variant needs no id.

NOT CHECKED
- Behaviour as a non-root builder. By reading, the store's 0444 manifest would then give EACCES, while files the builder owns with write permission stay exposed.
- The full journey through the web interface.

SUGGESTED FIX
The first reviewer's fix is sound. The smallest version:
- refuse a history that names EXPORT-NOTE.txt at line 82, alongside `acceptance`;
- write both files with an exclusive, no-follow create (`flag: "wx"`, which does not follow a link at the last component) after an lstat;

**What I ran** (probes in <scratchpad>/rev14-chal-gitig/probes/probe.mts and <scratchpad>/rev14-chal-gitig/probes/probe2.mts; no database, no container):

| Engine-written file in the history | writeExport | What the export's last commit holds |
|---|---|---|
| none, or the template's own .gitignore (controls) | succeeds | all four: EXPORT-NOTE.txt, README.txt, item-01.spec.ts, manifest.json |
| .gitignore: `/acceptance/**/*.spec.ts` + `/acceptance/README.txt` | succeeds | EXPORT-NOTE.txt and manifest.json only |
| .gitignore: `/acceptance/*` | succeeds | EXPORT-NOTE.txt only |
| .gitignore: `node_modules/` + `*.spec.ts` (an ordinary-looking rule) | succeeds | no test; README.txt and manifest.json are there |
| .gitignore: `EXPORT-NOTE.txt`, `acceptance/` or `*` | fails at `git add` | no archive written |

In the three silent cases the commit subject still reads "[export] acceptance v001 ... and the export note", `git status` in the extracted copy is clean, the loose files are in the archive, and a fresh clone lacks whatever the rule ignored.

**What I read:**
- builder/src/orchestrator/export.ts:121-125: a plain `git add -- acceptance EXPORT-NOTE.txt`, and nothing afterwards compares the commit with the manifest. `files` is returned but only counted.
- builder/src/orchestrator/journey-jobs.ts:593-597: `workspace_history_changed: false` and `acceptance_in_exported_copy_only: true` are written as constants.
- builder/src/engine/scripted.ts:50-64: `.gitignore` and `.gitattributes` are not protected paths. templates/next/.gitignore exists and is tracked.
- builder/test/journey.test.ts:706 checks the commit's four files on the normal path only; no test has a hostile ignore file.
- builder/scripts/demo-journey.ts:326-334 checks the `tar` listing only, which passes on loose files.

**Why not blocking:**
- It cannot happen with today's scripted engine. The three manifests (two steps and the broken copy) write neither `.gitignore` nor `.gitattributes`, and the template's own rules match none of the export's files.
- So the event's constant is true in every run that can happen at this commit, and J1's "downloads the export" is met. No hard rule is broken today.

**Why not minor:**
- The task's threat model treats the engine's files as hostile, and docs/design/journey-j1.md (build brief) names the export's copy of the tests as acceptance separation to be reviewed adversarially.
- A file the engine writes decides, silently, whether the tests and the stand-in README reach the exported history, while the commit message and the record say they did.
- It has no test and no known gap, so nothing would stop package 2.2 inheriting it.

**Corrections to the finding as stated:**
1. "Fails with a raw git error" overstates what the owner sees. The job's recorded reason is "the job stopped with an error (Error)" (builder/src/orchestrator/journey.ts:1143); git's text goes only to the fault log. The owner is still left unable to export, with no reason on the screen.
2. The export screen's sentence ("with the checklist's tests added in the copy only, as one .tar.gz file") stays literally true of the archive. What becomes false is the commit message and the design's "committed in the exported copy only" (journey-j1.md, item 9).
3. `git add -f` alone would not close it. I also ran two `.gitattributes` cases, where the export succeeds with all four files committed:
   - `acceptance/**/*.spec.ts working-tree-encoding=UTF-16LE`: the test as the commit's own object holds it differs from the manifest's SHA-256.
   - `acceptance/** text eol=crlf`: the commit's object matches, but a fresh clone's file differs.

   The fix therefore needs the check from the commit's own objects, as the finding suggests, plus attributes neutralised for the export's add (or `.gitattributes` treated like `.gitignore`), and a test for each.

**Not looked at:** the full journey through the web interface with a real sandbox; I called writeExport directly.

findings.title: A named pipe left in the app camera's output folder stops the whole interface
findings.file_line: <scratchpad>/wtrev14/builder/src/orchestrator/journey-jobs.ts:618-622 (readShot; called at :527). Same open-then-check pattern in <scratchpad>/wtrev14/builder/scripts/demo-journey.ts:97-103, demo-journey-j2.ts:124-128, demo-journey-j3.ts:77-83 and :101-107, and <scratchpad>/wtrev14/builder/src/web/files.ts:81
findings.what: readShot opens each expected screenshot with O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW and only afterwards checks that it is a plain file. Opening a named pipe for reading waits until something opens it for writing; the camera's container has ended by then, so the wait never ends. The call is synchronous inside the interface's one process, so every screen and every job of every project stops until someone kills the process by hand. The function's own comment says only plain files are read. The acceptance side does not have this: results.ts:97-109 checks with lstat before it reads.
findings.scenario: Precondition: code running as the runner's user (uid 1001) inside the camera's container. Page content alone did not get there in my tries (see what held); it needs the camera's browser taken over, and that browser runs without its own sandbox (gap 70). Today the app is built from fixed changes, so this matters from the point where page code written by a model runs in that browser (package 2.3). RAN, three parts: (1) in the real app camera container, started by example1Sandboxes().appCamera with the real compose file, `mkfifo /shots/zz-probe-pipe` as uid 1001 succeeded and the pipe was in the output folder on the machine afterwards (<scratchpad>/rev14-mounts/run-all.txt, line 'inside, named pipe'); (2) readShot on a named pipe did not return in 20 s (killed by timeout), while a link was refused at once; (3) the real JourneyJobs.appShots, given a stand-in camera that left app-home-en.png as a named pipe and ended with exit code 0: a 1-second timer in the same process never fired in 12 s, and the kernel showed the process waiting in wait_for_partner; the control with plain files went straight on to record the first screenshot (<scratchpad>/rev14-mounts/d/probe-appshots.mts, run-pipe.txt). READ only: files.ts:81 has the same pattern but I found no container that can write its folders at the time a file is served.
findings.suggested_fix: Check with lstat first and refuse anything that is not a plain file, as results.ts does, or open with O_NONBLOCK added and then fstat. Add a fast test that leaves a named pipe at an expected name (test/scripted-engine.test.ts already has an mkfifo helper for the workspace). Apply the same to readPng and takeSecret in the three demo scripts and to files.ts.
findings.known_gap: None covers it. Gap 70 records the precondition (the browser's own sandbox is off). Gap 71 says the builder reads only plain files, but for the runner's /results.

findings.what: Not a camera mount, but it is in the files part of this lens (another project's files). The J1 run removes only folders that appeared during the run, which can still be another interface's. The script itself plans for the owner's interface being up at the same time (:150 'the owner's project may hold it', :153 'The owner's interface on 4020 is not touched').
findings.scenario: The owner's interface has a project between steps (step 1 built, waiting for approval). The J3 run is started in a session that uses the same temporary folder (the default /tmp when TMPDIR is not set; which one the owner's interface uses is not recorded and I did not check it). findings.title: The J3 automated run writes into the builder camera's folder as root, through a link, and gives the target to the runner's user
findings.file_line: <scratchpad>/wtrev14/builder/scripts/demo-journey-j3.ts:313-314 (the folder is mounted read-write at /shots at :222)
findings.what: After the live camera's walk, the run writes the marker file live-done into camera-out with writeFileSync and then chownSync, both of which follow links. camera-out belongs to uid 1001 and is the builder camera's /shots, so a process inside that container can put a link named live-done there first. The run, as root, then overwrites the link's target with 'done' and makes uid 1001 its owner. Every read from the same folder is careful (O_NOFOLLOW); this one write is not.
findings.scenario: RAN (a replay of the two lines, in my scratch folder): with camera-out/live-done a link made as uid 1001 to a root-owned file of mode 600 inside a root-only folder, the two lines left that file holding 'done' and owned by 1001 (<scratchpad>/rev14-mounts/b/replay.mjs). RAN in a real camera container (the app camera's, whose /shots mount is the same kind): uid 1001 made a link in /shots to /etc/passwd and it was there on the machine afterwards. Precondition: code running inside the builder camera's container. That camera loads only the builder's own pages (escaped text and PNG pictures); I found no way for a hostile app to get code there short of two browser flaws in a row, which is why this is minor. The effect if it happened is the largest of anything here: any file on the machine overwritten and handed to the runner's user.
findings.suggested_fix: Create the marker with flag 'wx' plus O_NOFOLLOW (fails on anything already there) and set the owner on the open descriptor (fchown) or with lchown; or put the marker in a folder the camera sees read-only.
findings.known_gap: None.

findings.title: The J1 automated run reads the downloaded export through a link and with no size limit
findings.what: The run reads camera-out/export.tar.gz with existsSync, readFileSync and `tar -tzvf`, all of which follow a link, and none of which checks for a plain file or a size. The SHA-256 is printed into run-demo.txt and tar's listing is written into export-contents.txt in the evidence folder. The screenshots from the same folder are read carefully (readPng); the export is not.
findings.scenario: RAN (a replay of those calls in my scratch folder): with export.tar.gz a link made as uid 1001 to an archive in a root-only folder, the replay printed that archive's SHA-256 and its full listing of names (<scratchpad>/rev14-mounts/c/replay.mjs). READ: a named pipe or /dev/zero there would hang the run or exhaust its memory. Same precondition as the finding above (code inside the builder camera's container), and the run would then fail its own SHA comparison, so the cost is a leak of names and one fingerprint into evidence, or a stuck run.
findings.suggested_fix: Read it as the screenshots are read: no link followed, a plain file, a size cap; then give tar the bytes on its standard input.
findings.known_gap: None.

findings.title: Nothing limits what a camera leaves in its output folder, and a deep tree makes the clean-up throw
findings.what: /shots is a folder on the data folder's disk, mounted read-write, with no limit on size, count or depth. The reader refuses a file over 20 MB, but only after it has been written. The clean-up in `finally` is Node's rmSync, which cannot remove a tree deeper than the machine's path limit; its error then replaces whatever appShots was about to return, and the run folder stays.
findings.scenario: RAN, page content only: the real app camera, pointed at a hostile stand-in page 1,280 by 16,402 px of random pixels, wrote a 63,128,137-byte app-home-en.png to the machine; readShot refused it ('not a plain file of 8 bytes to 20 MB'). A page of 49,000 px crashed the camera's page instead (exit code 1). So a page alone costs tens of MB per picture, for the length of one run. RAN, in my scratch folder: rmSync({recursive, force}) on a run folder whose out/ held 40 nested folders with 200-character names threw ENAMETOOLONG on Node 22.23.4 and left the folder, its secret file included; `rm -rf` removed it. READ: that throw happens inside appShots' `finally` (:545), so a preview whose four screenshots were already recorded would still end as failed. Making such a tree, or filling the disk, needs code inside the camera's container.
findings.suggested_fix: Record the cameras under gap 58 or a new gap. In the camera script, clip the picture's height. In the `finally`, catch the error, report a fault and fall back to a removal that copes (gap 58 names `rm -rf`). For the server profile, put the output folder on something with a size limit.
findings.known_gap: Gap 58 is the same family (no limit, and a tree rmSync cannot remove), but for the engine's workspace only; the cameras are not named there or in gap 138.

findings.title: A hard stop during a camera run leaves the run folder, with the sample password file, in the data folder for good
findings.what: The run folder <data>/journey/<project>/camera-runs/run-<id> (out/ and secret/sample-password, mode 0400, uid 1001) is removed only by this function's own `finally`. If the interface is killed while the camera runs, nothing removes it later: no start-up recovery, no project close and no other code names camera-runs.
findings.scenario: READ only: a search of builder/src, scripts and test finds camera-runs at journey-jobs.ts:490 and in three test assertions, nowhere else; main.ts and journey.ts remove nothing under the data folder. The password is made up and its sandbox is removed at the next start, so today the cost is a stray file per hard stop.
findings.suggested_fix: At start-up, remove every <data>/journey/*/camera-runs/* (no camera can be running then), or hand the password to the container on its standard input so no file exists.
findings.known_gap: Gap 139 covers sandboxes left by a stopped interface, not this folder in the data folder.

findings.title: No fast test pins the live camera's or the builder camera's mounts, and the acceptance service accepts any mount
findings.what: The app camera's mount list is pinned by a test without containers (test/journey.test.ts:1174). The live camera's list is not: dropping ':ro' from /psock or /run/secrets/live, or adding a wider mount, would fail no fast test, and the live test would most likely still pass. The builder camera's docker arguments are written out three times in three scripts, with no test. findings.scenario: READ only: a search of builder/test for 'live-shots.mjs', '/run/secrets/live', 'psock:ro' and 'builder-shots.mjs:/camera' finds only test/isolation.test.ts:941, which passes its own mount to its own probe and does not call liveCamera. challenge.reasoning:
I tried to refute it and could not. The finding is real as stated, is not blocking, and no known gap records it.

WHAT I RAN (my own probes, scratch folder <scratchpad>/rev14-fifo/, probe.mts and fifo-out.txt):
1. The real readShot, imported from <scratchpad>/wtrev14/builder/src/orchestrator/journey-jobs.ts, inside a process with a 1-second timer and a SIGTERM handler (as the interface has at src/web/main.ts:461-462).
   - Controls: a plain PNG was read (18 bytes); a link, a folder, a socket and a missing file were each refused at once with JourneyRefused, and the timer kept firing.
   - Named pipe: "calling readShot" was the last line. No timer fired in the next 10 s. /proc/<pid>/stack showed the main thread in fifo_open -> wait_for_partner.
2. One thing worse than the finding says: SIGTERM had no effect. The process was still alive 5 s later and its handler never ran; only SIGKILL ended it. So the interface's clean stop (stopOnSignal, which removes sandboxes and releases the instance lock) cannot run from this state. "Kill by hand" means kill -9; the project's containers then stay until the next start's recovery.
3. Can the camera's container make the pipe? Yes. In a container I created and removed (builder-acceptance-runner:local, --user 1001:1001, --read-only, --cap-drop ALL, no-new-privileges, --network none, a folder owned by 1001 mounted at /shots), `mkfifo /shots/app-home-en.png` succeeded and the pipe was on the machine afterwards, owned by 1001. The read-only root and dropped capabilities do not prevent it. Mine was a plain docker run, not the project's compose service; the first reviewer's run-all.txt (lines 24 and 81) shows the same through the real service.

WHAT I READ
- journey-jobs.ts:618-627: open with O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW first, fstat/isFile only afterwards. Line 527 calls it directly in appShots after the camera has ended (`await r.done`, src/orchestrator/example-1-adapter.ts:304-318), so no writer exists. Nothing checks the entry's type before the open.

finding.title: The J3 automated run removes every sandbox folder in the temporary folder, not only its own
finding.file_line: <scratchpad>/wtrev14/builder/scripts/demo-journey-j3.ts:401-402 (start check :144-150; the interface is given the shared TMPDIR at :182). Weaker form in <scratchpad>/wtrev14/builder/scripts/demo-journey.ts:376-381 (TMPDIR at :192)
finding.what: Not a camera mount, but it is in the files part of this lens (another project's files). At the end of the J3 run, every folder in the temporary folder whose name starts builder-acceptance- (except the stand-ins) is removed with rmSync, with no list of what was there before and no check of who made it. The prefix also matches the tests' own folders (builder-acceptance-gate-, -data-, -probe-, -fast-). The J1 run removes only folders that appeared during the run, which can still be another interface's. The script itself plans for the owner's interface being up at the same time (:150 'the owner's project may hold it', :153 'The owner's interface on 4020 is not touched').
finding.scenario: The owner's interface has a project between steps (step 1 built, waiting for approval). The J3 run is started in a session that uses the same temporary folder (the default /tmp when TMPDIR is not set; which one the owner's interface uses is not recorded and I did not check it). The run's start check refuses only when a journey container, image, volume or network exists; RAN: after one engine container run through sandbox.runStreaming and ended, the project had its sandbox folder and no container, network, volume or image (<scratchpad>/rev14-mounts/probe-engine-objects.mts), and its build port is free, so the run starts. At its end, lines 401-402 remove that project's folder: its workspace, its history (workspace.git), its compose file and its secrets. READ: lines 401-402 themselves; I did not run the whole J3 run. The recorded run removed none (evidence/2026-11-13-journey-j3/run-demo.txt:90), so the evidence is not wrong; the code is. J2's script already does this the right way (its interface gets a temporary folder of its own, and only folders under the run's own folder are removed: demo-journey-j2.ts:662).
finding.suggested_fix: As J2 does: give the run's interface a temporary folder inside the run folder, and remove only the folders the run's own events record (journey.sandbox.made) and that sit under it. Never list the shared temporary folder by name prefix. Until then, record it as a known gap and say in the script's header that it must not be run while another interface has a project.
finding.known_gap: None covers it. It sits close to hard rule 9's intent (nothing destroyed outside the run's own things), but the folders are the builder's, so I do not call it blocking.

challenge.already_known_gap: None covers it. The nearest are gap 136 (says the sandbox folder is in the interface's TMPDIR, and that the adapter removes only a j1- project's own folder; it says nothing about the run scripts) and gap 139 (a sandbox lives only in the interface process that made it). Neither records that the J3 run script removes folders by name prefix.
challenge.reasoning:
I could not refute it. The finding is real as stated, and I moved its central claim from READ to RAN. The severity holds, at the low end of serious; it is not blocking.

**What I ran**
- Probe: `<scratchpad>/rev14-chal-sweep/probe-sweep.mts`; output in `run-sweep.txt` beside it.
- It makes a sandbox through the adapter's own `make()` (`example1Sandboxes` in `builder/src/orchestrator/example-1-adapter.ts`), as an interface does for a project's first step, in a temporary folder of the probe's own.
- It then executes lines 401-402 of `<scratchpad>/wtrev14/builder/scripts/demo-journey-j3.ts`, read from the file, not retyped.
- Result: the other project's folder was removed whole (workspace, `workspace.git`, `compose.yaml`, `secrets/app.env` and `db_password`). Decoy `builder-acceptance-gate-` and `builder-acceptance-fast-` folders went too. Only `builder-acceptance-standin-` and an unrelated folder were kept.
- Before the sweep, Docker listed no container, image, volume or network naming that project, so the start check (`journeyLeftovers`, lines 144-150, Docker only) could not have refused.
- No container was started, the worktree is unchanged, and the probe's folder was removed.

**What I read to test the scenario**
- The sweep sits in the `finally` block, so it runs whatever the run's outcome.
- The spawned interface is given the script's own `TMPDIR` (line 182).
- The engine service is `network_mode: none` and runs with `--rm` (`builder/src/sandbox/manager.ts` 272, 786). A project between steps, or after a failed preview (`stopApp`), therefore has a folder and nothing in Docker. That agrees with the first reviewer's probe.
- Same temporary folder: the script header's command sets no `TMPDIR`. The documented start of the owner's interface (`evidence/2026-11-13-journey-j1/journey.md` line 87) lists no `TMPDIR` among its settings. `TMPDIR` is unset in this session's shell. So both default to `/tmp`.
- The J1 weaker form is as described: `demo-journey.ts` takes `foldersBefore` at line 138 and removes only new folders at 376-381.
- The recorded J3 runs removed none, so the evidence is not wrong.

**What weakens it (not enough to refute)**
- The repeated runs of 14 Nov exported a private scratch `TMPDIR` (the session's `repeat-runs.sh`), and gap 175 says the earlier J1 and J3 runs used scratch `TMPDIR`s of 93 to 97 bytes. In those runs an interface on `/tmp` would not have been hit. Nothing in the script or the docs requires that.
- I could not check which folder the owner's interface uses: none is running and its environment is not recorded.
- The loss is bounded: made-up data, a scripted build that can be redone, and by gap 139 a sandbox is already lost at any interface restart.
- Only projects with a folder and nothing in Docker are exposed; if the owner's app is running, the run refuses to start.

**Why it is not blocking**
- Hard rule 9: the folders carry the builder's own name prefix inside the temporary folder, so this is not a destructive command outside the project.
- J1's "Done means" clause "No container, image or folder of J1 left after it" is met.
- J3 has no finish item about the owner's interface, and 3.1b's four clauses concern the acceptance gate.

**Why I keep serious rather than minor**
- The run destroys another instance's state that it did not make, in the configuration the documented commands give.
- It does so silently: unlike J1's script, J3's sweep does not set the exit code, so the run would still end "every check passed".
- The log prints "The owner's interface on 4020 is not touched" unconditionally (line 153), which would then be untrue.
- The script was written to run alongside the owner's interface, and no known gap records the risk.
- In a shared scratch `TMPDIR` the same sweep breaks another run's `acceptance.test.ts` or `acceptance-gate.test.ts` scratch folders (a spurious red, not a false pass).

**Adjacent, read only, not part of this finding**
- The same clean-up block removes Docker containers, images, volumes and networks by the `builder_j1-` prefix, not by the run's own project id (J3 lines 389-397; `demo-journey.ts` 365-375). The start check covers this only at the start.

**Fix**
- The suggested fix is right and small: do as `demo-journey-j2.ts` does (interface `TMPDIR` inside the run folder at line 250; removal only under the run folder at line 662). Until then, record a known gap and a warning in the script's header.

**Not looked at**
- I did not run the whole J3 script.
- I did not trace what the owner's screens show after the folder vanishes.

findings.title: The cameras' own "refuse every other address" rule does not see a redirect's target or a WebSocket, and the check "nothing but ... was loaded" passes when another address was loaded
findings.file_line: builder/camera/builder-shots.mjs:43-49 and :704; builder/camera/live-shots.mjs:62-72 and :296; builder/camera/app-shots.mjs:33-37 (no rule at all); builder/scripts/demo-journey.ts:226 (--network host); evidence/2026-11-13-journey-j1/journey.md:154 and :205; builder/src/orchestrator/example-1-adapter.ts:27
findings.what: The builder camera and the live camera limit their browser with one Playwright rule: continue for the one allowed address, abort and count the rest. In Playwright 1.63.0 with this Chromium that rule is never asked about (a) the request a redirect leads to, for a page, an image, a fetch or a re-sent form POST, or (b) a WebSocket. Those go out uncounted, so the closing check (`outside.length === 0`) passes. The builder camera is the one camera on the machine's network, and it types the interface password into a form; the rule is the only thing the record names between it and every other address (gap 138: "every other address refused, and the count of refused requests checked"; journey.md:154: "It refused every address but 127.0.0.1:4020 inside the browser, and none was asked for"). What actually holds today is something the record does not name: the interface's content-security-policy (default-src 'none', img-src 'self', form-action 'self') and the fact that its redirects are fixed local paths. For the live camera it is the preview front's policy and its Location mapping. The app camera has no in-browser rule at all: example-1-adapter.ts:27 says "It loads only http://app:<port>", but its browser follows whatever the app's pages ask for; only the network limits it (see the next finding).
findings.scenario: RAN. In a container of my own from the approved runner image, started as demo-journey.ts starts the builder camera except `--network none`, with the cameras' rule copied word for word and three listeners on the container's own loopback: `docker run --rm --name rev14-netsec-browser-probe --network none --read-only --tmpfs /tmp:rw,noexec,nosuid,size=512m --cap-drop ALL --security-opt no-new-privileges:true --pids-limit 256 --memory 1g --user runner --workdir /runner --entrypoint node --volume <scratch>/browser-probe.mjs:/camera/browser-probe.mjs:ro builder-acceptance-runner:local /camera/browser-probe.mjs`. Script and output: <scratchpad>/rev14-netsec/browser-probe.mjs and <scratchpad>/rev14-netsec/browser-probe.out. Trial A (a page of the allowed address, no policy): the rule refused and counted the direct image, fetch and beacon; but `GET /ws` (WebSocket), `GET /via-image-redirect` and `GET /via-fetch-redirect` arrived at the other listeners, uncounted. Trial C (the allowed address answers a navigation with a 302 elsewhere): the browser ended at http://127.0.0.1:4999/via-navigation-redirect?carried=made-up, count of refused requests 0. Trial D (a form with a typed password field, answered with a 307 elsewhere): `POST /via-post-redirect` arrived at the other listener, count 0. Trial B (the same page under a policy like the interface's): nothing arrived elsewhere, which is why this is not reachable through the interface as written. READ: the interface's redirects (app.ts, `localPath` at :420-423) and the front's `mapLocation` (preview-rules.ts:349) give no off-site redirect today.
findings.known_gap: Partly gaps 138 and 154: both say the limit is inside the browser, not the network. Neither says the in-browser rule misses redirects and WebSockets, and gap 138's and journey.md's wording says every other address is refused.
findings.suggested_fix: Take the builder camera off the machine's network with the pattern J3 already built for the live camera: `--network none`, a socket folder mounted read-only (preview.ts `cameraSocket` pointed at the interface's port) and the in-container forwarder on 127.0.0.1:<port>; then "loads nothing else" is the network's doing (not run as a whole by me; its two halves each ran: J3's live camera, and loopback listeners in a `--network none` container in my probe). Until then: count from `context.on("request")` including `request.redirectedFrom()` hops and `page.on("websocket")`, set `serviceWorkers: "block"`, assert after every navigation that `page.url()` starts with the allowed address, and correct the wording of gaps 138 and 154, of journey.md:154 and :205, and of example-1-adapter.ts:27 to say what the rule does and that the interface's policy is what holds the rest.

findings.title: The check before the app camera and the live camera start reads the words of the compose file, not Docker's own network or container; it passes while the container lands on an ordinary network with a route to the machine
findings.what: `frontOnlyProblem` asks three things of `docker compose config`: the service names `front` alone, `front` says `internal: true`, and it carries the "isolated" gateway option. It does not ask (1) whether `front` is the project's own network: a `name:` on it passes, and Compose then uses any existing network of that name with only a warning; (2) `enable_ipv6` (the manager relies on `enable_ipv6: false`; no IPv6 gateway mode is set); (3) what Docker really made: no `docker network inspect`, no inspect of the started container, and no check of the Docker Engine version, though manager.ts:150 says the option needs Engine 28 or later; (4) anything else of the service: privileged, root, the Docker socket mounted, `pid: host`, another project's socket folder all pass, although the adapter's header says the camera runs with "its unprivileged user, its read-only root and its hardening". Since the app camera's browser has no rule of its own (previous finding), this check is the only guard before model-written pages run in it. Nothing hostile can write the compose file today (it sits in a root-only folder made by mkdtemp; the engine mounts only `workspace/`: read), so the realistic trigger is a later change to the manager, a different Docker, or a leftover network, not an attacker.
findings.scenario: RAN. (a) `npx tsx <scratchpad>/rev14-netsec/front-probe.mts` (output front-probe.out beside it): a sandbox folder in my scratch folder from the real `createSandbox`, the compose file rewritten per case, the real `cameraNetworkProblem` asked. Refused, as they should be: acceptance on front and out; network_mode host; front not internal; front without the isolated option; front external. Passed (null, "the camera would start"): front with `enable_ipv6: true`; front with `name: bridge`; front told to use the machine's docker0 bridge; acceptance privileged, root, Docker's socket mounted, pid host, no read-only root; another project's socket folder mounted; the app also on an ordinary network with a way out. (b) What Compose then does with a named front: in a tiny project of my own (.../rev14-netsec/c7b/compose.yaml: `front` with `name: rev14-netsec-plain`, internal true, the isolated option, IPv6 off) against an ordinary network I created (`docker network inspect`: internal=false, gateway 172.18.0.1), `frontOnlyProblem` gave null, Compose printed "a network with name rev14-netsec-plain exists but was not created by compose" and started the container there: addresses lo 127.0.0.1 and eth0 172.18.0.2, default route through 172.18.0.1 (c7b/run.out, run.err). My container and network were removed. With `name: bridge` Docker itself refused (aliases are not allowed on its default network): c7/run.err. Not measured: IPv6 (this machine's kernel has none); an Engine older than 28.
findings.known_gap: None says it. Nearest: gap 138 ("Compose's own reading of the service is checked", accurate wording), gap 140 (the image label is not a protection), gap 124 (IPv6 off by setting, not shown).
findings.suggested_fix: Check Docker's objects as well as the file. Before the start: refuse `name` and `external` on `front`, require `enable_ipv6 === false`, and `docker network inspect <project>_front` for Internal true, EnableIPv6 false, the isolated option, and the project's own Compose labels; refuse an Engine older than the one the option needs. After the container exists and before the script is let run (or by starting the camera with a fixed `docker run --network <project>_front ...` as the builder camera is started, not through the service): `docker inspect` its networks (exactly that one), Privileged false, its user, its mounts. Add test cases for a named front, IPv6 on and a privileged service.

findings.title: J3's automated run, as root, writes and then gives away a file named `live-done` inside the folder the builder camera's container can write, following a link
findings.file_line: builder/scripts/demo-journey-j3.ts:313-314 (and :169, :222 for the folder and its mount); builder/scripts/demo-journey.ts:321-326 (export.tar.gz read with links followed)
findings.what: Outside my lens strictly (it is a mount, found while following how the pass leaves the builder camera). `cameraOut` is given to uid 1001 and mounted read-write at /shots in the builder camera's container, which is running at that moment, waiting for /shots/live-done. findings.scenario: RAN as an emulation in my scratch folder, no container: a folder owned by 1001 holding a link `live-done` to a root-owned file of mode 600 elsewhere in my scratch folder, then the two lines of demo-journey-j3.ts:313-314 word for word under node as root. findings.title: The builder camera's browser runs with Chromium's own sandbox off, on the machine's network, with the interface password in a file its page processes could read; gap 138 does not say so
findings.what: `chromium.launch()` with no option starts the headless shell with `--no-sandbox` in every process. review.verdict: Nothing blocking in this lens: no hard rule is broken and no secret is printed, kept or readable by the app or the engine.
