finding.title: The cameras' own "refuse every other address" rule does not see a redirect's target or a WebSocket, and the check "nothing but ... was loaded" passes when another address was loaded
finding.file_line: builder/camera/builder-shots.mjs:43-49 and :704; builder/camera/live-shots.mjs:62-72 and :296; builder/camera/app-shots.mjs:33-37 (no rule at all); builder/scripts/demo-journey.ts:226 (--network host); evidence/2026-11-13-journey-j1/journey.md:154 and :205; builder/src/orchestrator/example-1-adapter.ts:27
finding.what: The builder camera and the live camera limit their browser with one Playwright rule: continue for the one allowed address, abort and count the rest. In Playwright 1.63.0 with this Chromium that rule is never asked about (a) the request a redirect leads to, for a page, an image, a fetch or a re-sent form POST, or (b) a WebSocket. Those go out uncounted, so the closing check (`outside.length === 0`) passes. The builder camera is the one camera on the machine's network, and it types the interface password into a form; the rule is the only thing the record names between it and every other address (gap 138: "every other address refused, and the count of refused requests checked"; journey.md:154: "It refused every address but 127.0.0.1:4020 inside the browser, and none was asked for"). What actually holds today is something the record does not name: the interface's content-security-policy (default-src 'none', img-src 'self', form-action 'self') and the fact that its redirects are fixed local paths. For the live camera it is the preview front's policy and its Location mapping. The app camera has no in-browser rule at all: example-1-adapter.ts:27 says "It loads only http://app:<port>", but its browser follows whatever the app's pages ask for; only the network limits it (see the next finding).
finding.scenario: RAN. In a container of my own from the approved runner image, started as demo-journey.ts starts the builder camera except `--network none`, with the cameras' rule copied word for word and three listeners on the container's own loopback: `docker run --rm --name rev14-netsec-browser-probe --network none --read-only --tmpfs /tmp:rw,noexec,nosuid,size=512m --cap-drop ALL --security-opt no-new-privileges:true --pids-limit 256 --memory 1g --user runner --workdir /runner --entrypoint node --volume <scratch>/browser-probe.mjs:/camera/browser-probe.mjs:ro builder-acceptance-runner:local /camera/browser-probe.mjs`. Script and output: <scratchpad>/rev14-netsec/browser-probe.mjs and <scratchpad>/rev14-netsec/browser-probe.out. Trial A (a page of the allowed address, no policy): the rule refused and counted the direct image, fetch and beacon; but `GET /ws` (WebSocket), `GET /via-image-redirect` and `GET /via-fetch-redirect` arrived at the other listeners, uncounted. Trial C (the allowed address answers a navigation with a 302 elsewhere): the browser ended at http://127.0.0.1:4999/via-navigation-redirect?carried=made-up, count of refused requests 0. Trial D (a form with a typed password field, answered with a 307 elsewhere): `POST /via-post-redirect` arrived at the other listener, count 0. Trial B (the same page under a policy like the interface's): nothing arrived elsewhere, which is why this is not reachable through the interface as written. READ: the interface's redirects (app.ts, `localPath` at :420-423) and the front's `mapLocation` (preview-rules.ts:349) give no off-site redirect today.
finding.known_gap: Partly gaps 138 and 154: both say the limit is inside the browser, not the network. Neither says the in-browser rule misses redirects and WebSockets, and gap 138's and journey.md's wording says every other address is refused.
finding.suggested_fix: Take the builder camera off the machine's network with the pattern J3 already built for the live camera: `--network none`, a socket folder mounted read-only (preview.ts `cameraSocket` pointed at the interface's port) and the in-container forwarder on 127.0.0.1:<port>; then "loads nothing else" is the network's doing (not run as a whole by me; its two halves each ran: J3's live camera, and loopback listeners in a `--network none` container in my probe). Until then: count from `context.on("request")` including `request.redirectedFrom()` hops and `page.on("websocket")`, set `serviceWorkers: "block"`, assert after every navigation that `page.url()` starts with the allowed address, and correct the wording of gaps 138 and 154, of journey.md:154 and :205, and of example-1-adapter.ts:27 to say what the rule does and that the interface's policy is what holds the rest.

challenge.already_known_gap: Partly. Gaps 138 and 154 already record that each camera's limit is inside the browser and not the network, and gap 138's risk column says the builder camera's container could reach the machine's services. Gap 148 records that navigation and WebRTC stay open in the owner's browser. No gap records that the rule misses a redirect's target and a WebSocket. Gaps 138 and 154, journey.md:154 and :205, builder-shots.mjs:6, live-shots.mjs:9 and docs/design/journey-j3.md:87 state the stronger property ("every other address refused").
challenge.reasoning:
I could not refute it. The mechanism reproduces, the cited lines are accurate, and it is not blocking. I keep serious-non-blocking, at the low end.

**What I ran.** My own probe, in my own container from builder-acceptance-runner:local with `--network none` (Playwright 1.63.0, Chromium 153.0.8010.12), with the cameras' rule copied word for word from builder-shots.mjs:43-49. Script and output: <scratchpad>/rev14-chal-j1cam/probe.mjs and <scratchpad>/rev14-chal-j1cam/probe.out.

| Trial | Result |
| --- | --- |
| 1. Page with no policy | Direct image and fetch to another listener were refused and counted (the rule's positive control). A WebSocket, an image redirect and a fetch redirect arrived at the other listeners uncounted. |
| 2. `goto` answered with a 302 elsewhere | Browser ended on the other listener's page; `outside.length === 0` still true. |
| 3. Under the interface's exact policy (app.ts:99-107) | Neither the image redirect nor a script's WebSocket arrived. |
| 4. Same policy, a link to a BASE path that answers 302 elsewhere | Browser ended on the other listener; the check passes. |
| 5 and 6. Same policy, form POST with a typed password field answered 303 and 307 elsewhere | Nothing arrived (`form-action 'self'`). |
| 7. Same policy, a direct link elsewhere | Refused and counted (positive control). |

Trial 4 sharpens the finding: the policy does not hold the navigation-redirect class at all. Only the interface's fixed redirect targets hold it.

`context.on("request")` saw every redirect hop and `page.on("websocket")` saw the WebSocket, so the suggested interim fix is workable.

**What I read.**
- builder/node_modules/playwright-core/lib/coreBundle.js:36251 continues a request that has `redirectedFrom` without creating a route.
- Every `c.redirect` in src/web/app.ts (lines 154 to 374, and `act`) goes to a fixed local path or through `localPath` (:420).
- src/web/preview-rules.ts: `mapLocation` (:349) passes local paths only; `refresh` and `link` are dropped (:266-267); the app policy has `connect-src 'self'` (:389).
- builder-shots.mjs navigates only to `${BASE}` pages in every walk.
- app-shots.mjs has no route rule; all three demo scripts start the builder camera with `--network host` (demo-journey.ts:226, demo-journey-j2.ts:321, demo-journey-j3.ts:216).

So nothing the engine, the app, or what they write can reach either blind spot today, as the finding itself says.

**Not blocking.**
- J1's "Done means" (docs/design/journey-j1.md section 3; the table at journey.md:126-146) has no item about what the camera loads.
- 3.1b's four clauses are unrelated.
- No hard rule is broken: the check ran and passed (rule 7), everything runs in containers (rule 9), and the over-broad wording sits inside gap entries marked Open.

**Why I did not lower it.** It is a demonstrated bypass of the only in-browser safeguard the record names, on the one camera with the machine's network. The evidence check passes with the browser sitting on another address. Several record lines state the stronger property and need correcting.

**What tempers it (not stated in the finding).**
- The builder camera is started only by scripts/demo-journey*.ts, never by builder/src.
- The password it types is a per-run random one for a throwaway interface on a fresh database that is dropped afterwards (demo-journey.ts:159, :384). It is not the owner's.
- The live camera and the app camera are on the project's `front` network alone, so the blind spots give them no reach beyond `front` even if they became reachable.

**Left behind.** Nothing: my container was removed (`--rm`, none listed afterwards), I created no database, and the worktree is untouched.

**Not looked at.** WebRTC, preconnect and prefetch in the camera browsers; the finder's "next finding" on the app camera's network.

finding.title: The check before the app camera and the live camera start reads the words of the compose file, not Docker's own network or container; it passes while the container lands on an ordinary network with a route to the machine
finding.what: `frontOnlyProblem` asks three things of `docker compose config`: the service names `front` alone, `front` says `internal: true`, and it carries the "isolated" gateway option. It does not ask (1) whether `front` is the project's own network: a `name:` on it passes, and Compose then uses any existing network of that name with only a warning; (2) `enable_ipv6` (the manager relies on `enable_ipv6: false`; no IPv6 gateway mode is set); (3) what Docker really made: no `docker network inspect`, no inspect of the started container, and no check of the Docker Engine version, though manager.ts:150 says the option needs Engine 28 or later; (4) anything else of the service: privileged, root, the Docker socket mounted, `pid: host`, another project's socket folder all pass, although the adapter's header says the camera runs with "its unprivileged user, its read-only root and its hardening". Since the app camera's browser has no rule of its own (previous finding), this check is the only guard before model-written pages run in it. Nothing hostile can write the compose file today (it sits in a root-only folder made by mkdtemp; the engine mounts only `workspace/`: read), so the realistic trigger is a later change to the manager, a different Docker, or a leftover network, not an attacker.
finding.scenario: RAN. (a) `npx tsx <scratchpad>/rev14-netsec/front-probe.mts` (output front-probe.out beside it): a sandbox folder in my scratch folder from the real `createSandbox`, the compose file rewritten per case, the real `cameraNetworkProblem` asked. Refused, as they should be: acceptance on front and out; network_mode host; front not internal; front without the isolated option; front external. Passed (null, "the camera would start"): front with `enable_ipv6: true`; front with `name: bridge`; front told to use the machine's docker0 bridge; acceptance privileged, root, Docker's socket mounted, pid host, no read-only root; another project's socket folder mounted; the app also on an ordinary network with a way out. (b) What Compose then does with a named front: in a tiny project of my own (.../rev14-netsec/c7b/compose.yaml: `front` with `name: rev14-netsec-plain`, internal true, the isolated option, IPv6 off) against an ordinary network I created (`docker network inspect`: internal=false, gateway 172.18.0.1), `frontOnlyProblem` gave null, Compose printed "a network with name rev14-netsec-plain exists but was not created by compose" and started the container there: addresses lo 127.0.0.1 and eth0 172.18.0.2, default route through 172.18.0.1 (c7b/run.out, run.err). My container and network were removed. With `name: bridge` Docker itself refused (aliases are not allowed on its default network): c7/run.err. Not measured: IPv6 (this machine's kernel has none); an Engine older than 28.
finding.known_gap: None says it. Nearest: gap 138 ("Compose's own reading of the service is checked", accurate wording), gap 140 (the image label is not a protection), gap 124 (IPv6 off by setting, not shown).
finding.suggested_fix: Check Docker's objects as well as the file. Before the start: refuse `name` and `external` on `front`, require `enable_ipv6 === false`, and `docker network inspect <project>_front` for Internal true, EnableIPv6 false, the isolated option, and the project's own Compose labels; refuse an Engine older than the one the option needs. After the container exists and before the script is let run (or by starting the camera with a fixed `docker run --network <project>_front ...` as the builder camera is started, not through the service): `docker inspect` its networks (exactly that one), Privileged false, its user, its mounts. Add test cases for a named front, IPv6 on and a privileged service.

challenge.already_known_gap: None records it as such. Parts are covered: gap 123 (a container mounting another project's socket folder by a manager mistake; its own fix line asks for a mount check), gap 124 (IPv6 off by setting, not shown), gap 125 and 128 (limits of the isolation evidence). Gap 140 records the same shape for the runner image (checked by name, then Compose starts whatever has that name, for "something that can use the machine's Docker"); the network analogue is not written down. Gap 138 words the check accurately ("Compose's own reading of the service is checked"), so no record claims more than is done.
challenge.reasoning:
The facts hold, but the severity does not: I could confirm the mechanism, not that it is serious, so I lower it to minor (hardening plus one missing known-gap line).

**What I confirmed**

- **Read:** `frontOnlyProblem` (`builder/src/orchestrator/example-1-adapter.ts:186-203`) reads only three things from `docker compose config`: the service is on `front` alone, `front` is `internal`, and it carries the isolated gateway option. It does not read `name`, `enable_ipv6`, or anything else of the service. Nothing in `builder/src/sandbox/manager.ts` or the adapter inspects Docker's network or container, reads the Engine version, or acts on Compose's warning.
- **Ran** (my own probe, under the shared lock; everything I made was removed): the mechanism is slightly wider than the finding says. With `front` written exactly as the manager writes it (no `name:` key), I pre-created a plain network under the default name `rev14chal_front` (internal=false, gateway 172.18.0.1).
  - `frontOnlyProblem` answered null.
  - Compose printed only "a network with name rev14chal_front exists but was not created by compose" and started the service there: eth0 172.18.0.2, default route via 172.18.0.1.
  - Control, no network beforehand: Compose made `front` itself with internal=true, the isolated option and its own labels; the container got 172.18.0.1 and no default route.
  - Output: `<scratchpad>/rev14-chal-j1cam/probe.out`.
- So refusing `name:` alone, as the suggested fix lists first, would not close it; only inspecting Docker's network (labels, Internal, Options) would.

**Why it is not serious**

1. **No hostile party can cause any of the conditions.** The compose file sits in a root-only `mkdtemp` folder (`builder/scripts/example-1-sandbox.ts:60`); the engine mounts only `workspace`, an empty folder and the change sets (`manager.ts:284-286`); no project container has Docker's socket. A foreign network under `builder_j1-<12 random hex>_front` needs Docker access on the machine, which is already root-equivalent. The finding says this itself.
2. **"The only guard" is wrong.** The primary guard is the manager writing every project network from one constant, and that output is pinned exactly by `builder/test/sandbox.test.ts:120-150`: `toEqual` on each network (an added `name` or `enable_ipv6: true` fails), each service's network list, `cap_drop`, `security_opt`, no ports. A later manager change would fail there first. The camera check is a second reading of the same file.
3. **The camera check is not the relevant control for a foreign network.** The app and database would land on it at `up`, long before the camera starts.
4. **No record overstates the check.** The adapter header, the `Sandboxes` comments and gap 138 all say "Compose's own reading".
5. **Sub-point 4 is outside a network check.** Privileged, root, Docker's socket and `pid: host` are pinned by the manager's tests, and the socket-folder case is gap 123.
6. **The Engine-version point is real but not hostile-controllable.** This machine runs 29.9.2, and `docs/SOURCES.md:298-300` records the Engine 28 requirement. From my memory of Docker's source, not measured: Engine 27 refuses the unknown mode, and only 26 or earlier would ignore it silently.

**Blocking test:** no hard rule is broken (containers only; no false claim; no check weakened). It is no item of J1's "Done means" (`docs/design/journey-j1.md:33`) or of 3.1b's four clauses.

**Proportionate response**

- Add a known-gap line, the network twin of gap 140: the check reads Compose's reading, not Docker's objects; a network of that name made by anything else with Docker access is used with only a warning (measured); nothing checks the Engine is 28 or later.
- Optionally, before the cameras and streams start, `docker network inspect <project>_front` for Internal true, the isolated option and the project's Compose labels, and have the check also require `enable_ipv6 === false`.

**Not re-measured:** IPv6 (this kernel has none), an Engine older than 28, and the first reviewer's cases 5 and 8 to 12, which I read from their output only.

review.area: Package 3.1b, "browser acceptance required": when an acceptance run counts as PASSED (merged code, commit 839be17, working copy wtrev14)

findings.title: The gate's settings rule is a list of names: three settings it does not name let `npm test` exit 0 with tests left out, and silence the gate itself
findings.what: The scan fails only if vitest.config.ts names passWithNoTests, allowOnly, exclude, include, filter, projects, dir, root or workspace. Other settings do the same job and are not named: `testNamePattern` (every test whose name does not match is skipped), `retry` (a test that fails and then passes counts as passed), `setupFiles` (a file that runs before every test file and can change what a check does). With any of them the scan returns nothing. The gate is also one of the tests it guards, so a name filter skips the gate test too. This is not a false pass today: the real vitest.config.ts holds none of these (read), and the suite holds none of the skip forms the scan misses (searched). It is a hole in the guard that finish criterion (1) rests on ("no test in the suite can be skipped").
findings.scenario: RAN. Made-up builder folders under <scratchpad>/rev14-falsepass/gate/mu-*, each with three tests: a failing "browser check", a passing test, and a test that fails on its first two tries. scanRunnerSettings and scanForLeftOutTests (imported from the working copy's test/gate-scan.ts) returned [] for all four. `vitest run`: plain settings: exit 1, 2 failed. `testNamePattern: "another made-up"`: exit 0, "1 passed | 2 skipped". `retry: 2`: exit 0, the twice-failing test counted as passed. `setupFiles` naming a file that redefines the matchers: exit 0, "3 passed". Probe: <scratchpad>/rev14-falsepass/probe-gate.ts (each mu-* folder needs a node_modules link to run again; I removed the links afterwards).
findings.known_gap: 112 in part. It records that the scan reads words and lists the settings it names, and says a later change could leave a check out in a way the scan does not read. It does not say that other settings (testNamePattern, retry, setupFiles) do the same, nor that a setting which leaves out the gate file silences the gate.
findings.suggested_fix: Turn the settings rule round: fail unless the settings file's `test` block holds only the three settings in use (fileParallelism, testTimeout, hookTimeout) and nothing else (no plugins, setup files or aliases). Add testNamePattern, retry and setupFiles to the made-up-folder test either way. Say in gap 112 that the gate cannot guard against a change that leaves the gate out; only a check outside the suite could (for example a small script after `vitest run` that reads the runner's own JSON report and fails on any skipped, to-do or retried test).

findings.title: A version whose tests cover 1 of 6 checklist items reads "passed"; the untested items change only the summary's text
findings.what: A checklist item with no test in the version is not in the reading at all. `checklistItems` is used only to add "checklist incomplete (5 of the app spec's 6 checklist items have no test)" to the summary. The outcome word stays "passed", the finished event has no field for the untested count, and sign-off reads only the word. `checklistItems` is the caller's number and is not compared with the version's own record (`checklist_items` in acceptance.version.written): given 0, the summary is plain "version passed". A manifest item with no test in the results is handled correctly: that item is "did not run" and the run is "not passed".
findings.scenario: RAN: <scratchpad>/rev14-falsepass/probe-results.ts, cases 01, 64 (PASSED, "checklist incomplete (5 of ... 6)"), 65 (checklistItems 0: PASSED, "version passed"), 60 (two manifest items, one with no test in the results: NOT PASSED). READ: journey.ts:656 allows sign-off on the word alone; the sign-off label and the checklist screen say "stand-in test of item 1 only".
findings.known_gap: 111 (not new): "an app could be shown 'passed' with most of its checklist untested"; whether an incomplete checklist may be called passed is the owner's question for package 3.2b. Not in 111: the caller-supplied count is unchecked, and the event carries no count.
findings.suggested_fix: Until the owner decides: put the untested count into the acceptance.run.finished event as its own field, taken from the version's own record and not from the caller, so that anything reading the record can tell "passed, 1 of 6 tested" from "passed, all tested" without reading the summary's text.

findings.title: A pass needs a "screenshot" that is only a file name: an empty file counts, and a real test that opens no browser is read as passed
findings.file_line: builder/src/acceptance/results.ts:344-357 and :117-123 (attachmentFile); :339-343 (the trace is kept if there, never required)
findings.what: For "passed" the reader requires exactly one attachment named item-screenshot whose path is a plain file under /results. It checks nothing about the file: not that it is an image, not that it has any bytes, not that it is this item's own file. No trace is required. So the one sign that a page was opened can be an empty file. The interface's own file server is stricter (builder/src/web/files.ts: at least 8 bytes, starting as a PNG does), so such an item would show "passed" with a picture that cannot be served.
findings.scenario: RAN, two ways. (a) Real Playwright 1.63.0 in the runner image, in a container I created (no network, removed after): a test that opens no page and attaches an empty file as item-screenshot ended with exit 0 and was read PASSED (<scratchpad>/rev14-falsepass/pw/c09-no-browser-empty-shot; reader run by probe-real.ts). (b) Crafted files, probe-results.ts: an empty file (71), a text file (72, 79), the results file itself named as the screenshot (73), one file used for two items (68): all PASSED. A missing file, a link, a path outside /results, the attachment given twice or inline: not passed.
findings.known_gap: 111 ("a test that passes without opening a page would still count") and 71 (a test written to cheat can claim a pass). Neither says that the screenshot's content is not checked; 111's proposed remedy ("no trace or screenshot") would not catch this case if it only asks that the attachment exists, which the reader already does.
findings.suggested_fix: At reading time, require the screenshot to start as a PNG does and to be at least a set size (the check web/files.ts and journey-jobs.ts readShot already make), to be a file no other item names and not results.json, and require the trace attachment with at least one trace entry (probes.ts already reads a trace's entries). Add the empty-file case to the "did not run" table in test/acceptance.test.ts.

findings.title: Exit code 1 with a report in which every test passed is read as "passed"
findings.what: The reader lets exit codes 0 and 1 through to the results file (1 is needed to read a failure), and then decides "passed" from the file alone. When the runner's own verdict (exit 1: something went wrong) and its file (everything passed, no error) disagree, the run is still recorded "passed", with exit_code 1 beside it in the same event.
findings.scenario: RAN. Reader: probe-results.ts case 02: PASSED. Whole chain (runAcceptance with a stand-in in place of the container, real test database, real image check): the acceptance.run.finished event holds exit_code=1 and outcome "passed", and the journey's runOutcome reads "passed" (<scratchpad>/rev14-falsepass/probe-chain.mts). I did not find a natural way to this pair: in 21 real Playwright runs in the runner image, every exit 1 came with a failed test or an error outside any test, both of which the reader catches. It would take a results file not written by Playwright (gap 71) or a non-zero exit of docker compose's own after a clean run (not provoked).
findings.known_gap: None names it. Gap 71 covers the cheating-test way to it.
findings.suggested_fix: Record "passed" only with exit code 0. With exit code 1, no failed item and no run problem: "not passed: the runner ended with exit code 1 but its report records no failure". One line in readResults and one row in the test table.

findings.title: The reader does not refuse a manifest that names one file, or one item number, twice: one test then passes two items
findings.what: readRun maps each manifest item to the tests in its file and does not check that items are distinct. verifyVersion, which runs first in a real run, refuses a file named twice but not a number given twice, nor a number that disagrees with its file name. What stops it today is one step further back: the manifest must match the builder's own acceptance.version.written event, and writeVersion refuses duplicates when it writes. So this is a second lock missing, not an open door.
findings.scenario: RAN (reader alone): probe-results.ts case 61 (two items naming item-01.spec.ts, one passing test: PASSED, items 1 and 2 both passed) and case 62 (two items numbered 1: PASSED). READ: verifyVersion's checks and versionMatchesEvent (runner.ts:98-109).
findings.suggested_fix: In verifyVersion (and as a first check in readRun): refuse a number given twice and a number other than the NN of its file name; give the run "not passed" with that reason.

findings.title: If the runner's container cannot even be asked for, the run leaves no record at all
findings.what: When runStreaming throws before a container exists (a mount source gone, a container name Docker would not accept), runAcceptance throws after removing the password file. No acceptance.run.started, acceptance.item or acceptance.run.finished event is written and no report.json: the store holds a run folder and nothing that says "not passed". Not a false pass: nothing says "passed", and in the journey the checklist job is recorded as failed, which sign-off treats as not passed (journey.ts, fold of a failed job, read). But criterion (2)'s "a run whose runner could not start" is recorded "not passed" only for the refusals made before step 4.
findings.scenario: RAN: probe-chain.mts, last case: runStreaming made to throw; runAcceptance threw; the project's events were [acceptance.version.written] only.

finding.title: The gate's settings rule is a list of names: three settings it does not name let `npm test` exit 0 with tests left out, and silence the gate itself

challenge.reasoning:
I could not refute it. The facts hold when re-run, it is not blocking, and the claimed severity stands, though at the top of what the facts support.

**What I ran** (my own made-up folders, the real scan imported from the working copy's `builder/test/gate-scan.ts`, vitest 5.1.0 from the working copy's `node_modules`; no Docker, no database). Each settings file held the real three settings (`fileParallelism`, `testTimeout`, `hookTimeout`) plus one more. In every case `scanRunnerSettings` and `scanForLeftOutTests` returned `[]`, and `vitest list` still listed the file.

| Case | `vitest run` |
| --- | --- |
| Plain settings | exit 1, 2 failed, 1 passed |
| `testNamePattern: "another made-up"` | exit 0, "1 passed, 2 skipped (3)" |
| `retry: 2` alone, a passing test and one that fails twice | exit 0, "2 passed (2)" |
| `retry: 2` alone, with a test that always throws | exit 1, "(initial run, 1st retry, 2nd retry)" |
| `setupFiles` redefining the matchers | the twice-failing test passed; the throwing test still failed (exit 1) |
| `setupFiles` naming a file outside `test/` whose `beforeEach` leaves each test out through the test context | exit 0, "3 skipped (3)" |
| Model of the gate guarding itself: a made-up gate test running the real scan on its own folder, plain settings | gate test passed, exit 1 on the made-up browser check only |
| Same model with `testNamePattern` | exit 0, gate test and browser check both skipped |

**Two imprecisions in the finding; neither changes the conclusion.**
- Its `retry` folder also held `testNamePattern: "flaky|another"`, which the finding does not say. Retry alone does count a twice-failing test as passed, but it cannot hide a failure that always happens, such as a missing browser. So `retry` weakens checks in general (rule 7) but does not touch Done-means clause (1).
- Its `setupFiles` case reached "3 passed" only because its made-up browser check failed through a matcher. The real live tests fail by throwing (`needsPrerequisites`), which a matcher override does not silence. A set-up file can still leave throwing tests and the gate out, as the "3 skipped" row shows, so the claim holds.

**Attempts to refute that failed.**
- No other check reads the settings file or the run's output: there is no `.github` folder, and `builder/scripts/make-evidence.sh` only runs vitest.
- The real `builder/vitest.config.ts` holds only the three settings, so there is no false pass at commit 839be17, as the finding says.
- The only partial safeguard is by hand: the run summary shows "skipped" for the leave-out cases, and the evidence files record "none skipped". It shows nothing for `retry`.

**Known gap.** Gap 112 covers it only in part, as the finding says. It lists the nine named settings and its risk is general ("a later change could leave a required check out in a way the scan does not read"). Its "does not see" list names only skip spellings, early returns and tests with no check. Its mitigation ("a reviewer reads each new test against that list") does not cover a settings change, and nothing says the gate cannot guard against a change that leaves the gate out.

**Severity.**
- Not blocking: no hard rule is broken and no check is weakened at this commit. Clause (1) is met as merged: the live tests fail without their prerequisites and nothing in the suite is skipped. The outside review's item is met.
- Serious rather than minor: the hole is in the guard clause (1) rests on, and a one-line, ordinary-looking setting (`retry`, `setupFiles`) in the very file the scan reads opens it. The same class of omission (`projects`, `dir`, `root`, `workspace`, `fails`) was fixed in code after the package's first review.
- What pulls towards minor: it needs a change to the builder's own repository, which the engine and the app cannot write, and whoever can make it could equally delete the gate.

**Fix.** The suggested fix is sound and has a precedent: `docs/DECISIONS.md`, 12 Nov, package 0.3, holds the template's `next.config.ts` to its exact contents by SHA-256 "because the settings can be written in too many ways to read reliably". Naming more settings would not be enough, because `test/acceptance-gate.test.ts:136-146` itself shows settings spread in from another file put no word in `vitest.config.ts`.

**Not looked at.** Command-line flags or environment variables that filter tests; other unnamed settings (`bail`, `alias`, plugins, `dangerouslyIgnoreUnhandledErrors`). I did not run the real gate test file or the whole suite, and did not change the real settings file.

**State left behind.** The working copy is unchanged (`git status` clean at 839be17). I created no database and no container. Probes are in `<scratchpad>/rev14-chal-list3/` (`probe.ts`, `probe2.ts`, `mu-*`). I removed the `node_modules/vitest` links, so each `mu-*` folder needs one to run again.
challenge.already_known_gap: Gap 112, in part. It records that the scan reads words, lists the nine settings it names, and gives the general risk that a later change could leave a check out in a way the scan does not read. It does not record that other settings (testNamePattern, retry, setupFiles) do the same, that its mitigation covers new tests but not settings changes, or that a setting which leaves the gate test out silences the gate. No other gap covers it.

challenge.reasoning:
The facts are real; I could not refute them. The severity is too high: the serious part is known gap 111 word for word, and the two details it adds are minor.

**What I confirmed (RAN)** — probe at <scratchpad>/rev14-chal-count/probe.ts, importing `readRun` from the worktree:
- Manifest [1], results [1], `checklistItems` 6: outcome "passed", summary "version passed; checklist incomplete (5 of the app spec's 6 checklist items have no test)".
- Same with `checklistItems` 0, 1, -3 or NaN: outcome "passed", summary plain "version passed".
- Manifest [1,2], results [1] only: "not passed", item 2 "did not run".
- Manifest []: "not passed".

**What I confirmed (READ)**
- `builder/src/acceptance/results.ts:383-386`: the count touches only the summary's text.
- `builder/src/acceptance/runner.ts:220-230`: `acceptance.run.finished` has no count field.
- `runner.ts:98-109` (`versionMatchesEvent`): compares the manifest fingerprint and items, not `checklist_items`.
- `builder/src/orchestrator/journey.ts:656`: sign-off reads only `refused` and the outcome word.

**Why the core is not new, and not blocking**
- Gap 111 (`docs/KNOWN-GAPS.md:127`, Open) states this case, quotes the same summary, and defers "whether an incomplete checklist may be called passed" to the owner at package 3.2b.
- 3.1b's own evidence lists it: `evidence/2026-11-13-package-3.1b/browser-required.md:81`, "Kept, recorded: known gap 111".
- It is the designed behaviour for J1: `docs/design/journey-j1.md:22` (section 1, item 8) and J1's finish list, `evidence/2026-11-13-journey-j1/journey.md:105-106`.
- Tests pin it: `builder/test/acceptance.test.ts:303-308`, `builder/test/acceptance-live.test.ts:109`.
- 3.1b's "Done means" clause 2 covers a runner that could not start or a run where no browser test ran. Here one did run, so the clause is met.
- Hard rule 7 is not broken: the one test counted ran and passed with its screenshot. Items 2 to 6 are shown "Did not run / No test written yet: did not run" (`builder/src/web/pages.ts:941-950`), not as passed.
- The sign-off button and the `signedOff` event carry "checked by a stand-in test of item 1 only: not acceptance" plus the summary (`journey.ts:258`, `:1052-1057`).

**Why the two new details are minor**
- **Unchecked caller count.** The only product caller is the builder's own code: `builder/src/orchestrator/journey-jobs.ts:566` passes `this.j.spec.acceptance.length`. That is the same example spec whose length `builder/src/acceptance/stand-in.ts:64` writes as `checklist_items`. Nothing the engine, app or runner container can write reaches it. A wrong number changes only text that no decision reads; the outcome is "passed" either way, which is gap 111.
- **No count in the finished event.** The record already tells "1 of 6" from "all tested" without parsing the summary. `acceptance.version.written` holds `checklist_items` and the tested `items` (`stand-in.ts:57-65`). The finished event links to it by `version` and `manifest_sha256`. The checklist screen uses exactly that to mark untested items (`pages.ts:919-921`, `:946`). The fix's stated reason is therefore overstated; a count field on the finished event would be a convenience.

The suggested fix is reasonable as a small hardening when 3.2b takes up gap 111: take the count from the version's own record.

**Not done:** no existing test, database or Docker was used. No file in the worktree was changed (`git status` clean).

finding.title: Settings the gate's scan does not name let `npm test` exit 0 with neither the gate test nor the live tests run
finding.what: The settings scan looks for nine words in vitest.config.ts (passWithNoTests, allowOnly, exclude, include, filter, projects, dir, root, workspace). Four other settings of vitest 5.1.0 leave tests out or turn a failure into a pass, and the scan says nothing about them: `testNamePattern` (every test whose name does not match is skipped, exit code 0), `changed` (on a clean git tree: "No changed files found, exiting with code 0", no test runs), `globalSetup` or `setupFiles` (a set-up file can end the run with exit code 0), and `retry` (a test that fails twice and passes the third time is reported passed). With the first three the gate test itself is among the tests left out, so nothing is there to fail: the gate cannot guard against its own deselection. At 839be17 the real vitest.config.ts has none of these (read), so the gate holds for the code as merged; this is about what a later change could do unseen.
finding.scenario: RAN, on made-up folders under <scratchpad>/rev14-gatebypass/cases, with the working copy's own scan functions and its vitest 5.1.0 (probe <scratchpad>/rev14-gatebypass/probes/scan-probe.ts, output scan-probe.out beside it). Each folder holds one passing test and one test that must fail (expect(1).toBe(2)). G, `testNamePattern: "plain"`: scan found nothing; vitest run exit code 0, "1 passed | 1 skipped". H, `changed: true`: scanRunnerSettings named nothing; vitest run exit code 0, "No changed files found, exiting with code 0". K, `globalSetup` whose file calls process.exit(0): scan found nothing; exit code 0, no test run. I, `retry: 3`: scan found nothing; a test that fails twice then passes: "2 passed", exit code 0. Control Z (a plain failing test): exit code 1. Control Y (the skip word written plainly): the scan found it.
finding.known_gap: Not covered. Gap 112 lists the nine settings the scan names and says nothing about settings it does not name; its "not seen" list is only about test files.
finding.suggested_fix: Stop reading words in the settings file: have the gate test compare vitest.config.ts with its exact expected text, so any new setting needs a visible change to the gate test. Because a setting can leave the gate test itself out, add a check that sits outside the tests it guards: for example a reporter named in that pinned settings file which fails the run unless the named live tests (7 in acceptance-live, 6 in preview-live) are present and passed, and no test ended skipped, to do, retried or as an expected failure. Until then, add these four settings to gap 112.

challenge.already_known_gap: Partly. Known gap 112 (docs/KNOWN-GAPS.md:128) already records the class and the consequence in the same words ("The gate's scan for left-out tests reads words"; "A later change could leave a required check out in a way the scan does not read"). It does not record these vectors: its "does not see" list is about test files only, its mitigation ("a reviewer reads each new test against that list") does not cover the settings file, and it says a left-out test file is seen "whatever setting leaves it out", which is not true for `changed` on a clean tree. So the finder's "not covered" is half right: the consequence is known, the four settings and the gate's own deselection are not written down.
challenge.reasoning:
I tried to refute it and could not: the behaviour holds, the finding is non-blocking, and two of its details need correcting.

WHAT I RAN (independent of the finder's probe; my own made-up folders under <scratchpad>/rev14-chal-settings/, outputs in run-controls.out and run-cases.out there). Each folder holds a copy of the working copy's own builder/test/gate-scan.ts, a gate test making the same four checks as builder/test/acceptance-gate.test.ts:88-95, one passing test and one test that must fail (expect(1).toBe(2)), and was run with the working copy's vitest 5.1.0 as `vitest run`. So, unlike the finder's probe, the gate test was inside the suite being run.
- Controls: plain settings with the must-fail test: exit code 1. Plain settings, all passing: exit code 0, gate test passed. `exclude` naming a test file: gate test failed, exit code 1. The stand-in gate works.
- G `testNamePattern: "plain"`: exit code 0, "1 passed | 2 skipped"; gate test and must-fail test both skipped.
- G2 `testNamePattern: "plain|the gate"`: exit code 0; the gate test RAN and PASSED while the must-fail test was skipped. Stronger than claimed: the scan passes even when it runs.
- H `changed: true`, clean git tree: exit code 0, "No changed files found, exiting with code 0", nothing ran. H2, same setting not yet committed: every test ran and the gate test passed (it does not name `changed`), so the change is not caught before the commit either.
- I `retry: 3`: exit code 0; gate test passed; a test that fails twice then passes is reported passed.
- K `globalSetup` whose file calls process.exit(0): exit code 0, nothing ran.
- K2 `setupFiles` whose file skips every test but one through the test context: exit code 0, "1 passed | 2 skipped", gate test among the skipped.

WHAT I READ. builder/vitest.config.ts at 839be17 sets only fileParallelism and two time limits, so the gate holds for the code as merged (the finder says so too). gate-scan.ts:28 lists nine words; none matches testNamePattern, changed, globalSetup, setupFiles or retry. There is no CI file in the repository; `npm test` is run by development sessions.

CORRECTIONS TO THE FINDING.
1. `setupFiles`: "a set-up file can end the run with exit code 0" is true for globalSetup only. K3 (setupFiles calling process.exit(0)) gave exit code 1: "process.exit unexpectedly called". setupFiles still leaves tests out with exit code 0 by skipping them (K2), so the substance stands; the finder ran globalSetup only.
2. `retry` does not defeat the browser-required clause. builder/test/acceptance-live.test.ts:31 reads the prerequisites once and each of the 7 tests throws on every attempt, so they still fail with retries (read, not run). `retry` only lets an intermittent failure be reported as a pass.
3. For the real suite, a name pattern or set-up file must also leave out the gate's first test (acceptance-gate.test.ts:70-86), which would otherwise see the 7 live tests skipped in its child run. One pattern can do both, so this narrows the route, it does not close it.
4. Line reference: the scan's test is at acceptance-gate.test.ts:88-95, not 87-94.

SEVERITY. Not blocking: no hard rule is broken at 839be17 and the outside review's item and clause (1) of "Done means" hold for the settings as merged; every route needs a later edit to a 4-line tracked file. I keep serious-non-blocking, on the low side of it, because: one word in the settings (`changed: true`) makes `npm test` exit 0 with no test run; the scan passes even when it does run (G2, H2, I); and two project texts say more than is shown: gate-scan.ts:7-8 ("a setting that leaves a test file out is seen whatever it is called") and gap 112 ("whatever setting leaves it out"). What pulls it down: gap 112 already states the consequence; the parties this review treats as hostile cannot write the file (the engine container mounts only its workspace, builder/src/sandbox/manager.ts:284-286; the builder folder is mounted read-only elsewhere, :435, :464, :482; read, not probed); and whoever can edit the settings can equally delete the gate test. If the orchestrator counts a finding whose consequence is already an open gap as an extension of that gap, "minor" is a fair reading.

ON THE SUGGESTED FIX. Pinning vitest.config.ts to exact contents has a precedent in this project (docs/DECISIONS.md:68, 12 Nov: the template's next.config.ts held by SHA-256 "because the settings can be written in too many ways to read reliably"). But neither the pin nor a reporter named in that file is complete: my case L (process.exit(0) as the first line of vitest.config.ts, no setting named) gave exit code 0 with nothing run. Any check inside `vitest run` can be switched off from the settings file, so a complete answer needs something outside the run (a wrapper as the `npm test` command, which the scan at gate-scan.ts:86 currently forbids), or the limit must be written down. Minimum: add the four settings and the gate's own deselection to gap 112 and correct "whatever setting leaves it out".

NOT LOOKED AT. I did not run the real suite, the real acceptance-gate.test.ts or any existing test, and started no container and no database. I did not test other vitest settings (for example custom reporters or dangerouslyIgnoreUnhandledErrors), environment variables, or command-line arguments. The working copy is unchanged (git status empty at 839be17); no probe process is left.

finding.title: The scan misses eight ordinary ways of leaving a test out of a test file, beyond the two that gap 112 names
finding.file_line: builder/test/gate-scan.ts:17-22 (the two patterns) and :58-72 (which files are read)
finding.what: The scan reads each line for the words skip, skipIf, runIf, todo, only, fails after describe/it/test/suite/bench, or for `.skip(`. Gap 112 records that it does not see a name built at run time, the options form, an early return, or a test with no check. These further forms also pass the scan while the test runner leaves the test out with exit code 0: (1) a test with no body, `it("name")`, which the runner marks to do; (2) the context's skip taken out by name, `({ skip }) => { skip(); }`, in a test or in a beforeEach hook; (3) a line break between the API and the word (`describe` on one line, `.skipIf(...)` on the next); (4) the API under another name (`const live = test.extend({})`, or `import { it as check }`), then `live.skipIf`, `live.fails`, `check.runIf`, `check.todo`; (5) the word in a helper outside test/ (the scan reads test/ and the runner's listed files only, and the live tests already import helpers from src/ and scripts/); (6) a test written down only when the prerequisite is there (`if (missing.length === 0) { it(...) }`); (7) a table of cases that is empty when the prerequisite is missing (`it.each(missing.length ? [] : [...])`); (8) a per-test `{ retry: 2 }`. The real suite at 839be17 has none of these (searched; the only `.each` has a fixed table), and for acceptance-live.test.ts the gate's child run (7 of 7 must fail with the prerequisites missing) would catch forms 1 to 7 whatever their spelling. Every other test file, preview-live.test.ts included, relies on the word scan alone.
finding.scenario: RAN, same probes as above plus scan-probe2.ts (output scan-probe2.out), folders under .../rev14-gatebypass/cases and cases2. In each, the scan found nothing and `vitest run` gave exit code 0 while a test that must fail did not fail: A (context skip by name) "1 passed | 1 skipped"; M (the same in beforeEach) "1 passed | 2 skipped"; B (line break) "1 passed | 1 skipped"; C (other name) "1 passed | 1 expected fail | 2 skipped | 1 todo"; D (helper in src/) "1 passed | 1 skipped"; E (written only if) "2 passed (2)", the failing test absent; F (empty table) "2 passed (2)"; L (no body) "2 passed | 1 todo"; N (per-test retry) "2 passed (2)". J (the options form, already in gap 112) behaved the same, for comparison.
finding.known_gap: Gap 112 covers the principle ("the scan reads words") and two of the forms; forms 1 to 8 above are not in its list, and its planned handling ("a reviewer reads each new test against that list") would use an incomplete list. Note for whoever decides the package's state: "Done means" (1) says "no test in the suite can be skipped or marked to do". No test is skipped at 839be17 (the gate passes; the latest full run in evidence/2026-11-14-journey-j2-second-review/run-tests-full.txt shows 31 files, 790 passed of 790). That none can be is not enforced; under build plan section 3, step 8, the gap does not turn that clause into "tested".
finding.suggested_fix: Check at run time what the runner did, not what the files say: the same reporter as in the first finding (fail the run if any test ends skipped, to do, as an expected failure or after a retry, and if any named live test is missing from the results). Extend the gate's child run to every *-live.test.ts file. Until then, add forms 1 to 8 to gap 112.

challenge.reasoning:
Upheld on the facts, with two corrections, and lowered from serious-non-blocking to minor. I could not confirm "serious".

WHAT I RAN (my own made-up folders and probe, not the first reviewer's): <scratchpad>/rev14-chal-eight/probes/probe.ts, output in <scratchpad>/rev14-chal-eight/probes/probe.out. It calls scanForLeftOutTests and scanRunnerSettings from builder/test/gate-scan.ts on each folder, then runs `vitest run` there. No database, no container. The working copy is unchanged (git status empty).

CONFIRMED (the scan found nothing, exit code 0, a test that must fail did not fail):
- Form 1, a test with no body: "2 passed | 1 todo".
- Form 2, skip taken out of the context by name, in a test and in beforeEach: "1 passed | 1 skipped" each.
- Form 3, a line break before skipIf, runIf, todo, fails: "1 passed | 1 expected fail | 2 skipped | 1 todo".
- Form 4, `test.extend({})` and `import { it as check }`: the same result.
- Form 5, `describe.skipIf` in a helper under src/: "1 passed | 1 skipped".
- Form 6, a test written only if the prerequisite is there: "2 passed (2)", the failing test absent.
- Form 7, an empty table for it.each: "2 passed (2)".
Controls: a plain failing test gives exit code 1; the plain word is found.

CORRECTION 1: form 8 is not a way of leaving a test out. A test given `{ retry: 2 }` that fails every time still fails (my case f8b: exit code 1, "1 failed"). The first reviewer's case N passed only because its made-up test is written to pass on the third try. Retry hides a failure that comes and goes; it cannot hide a missing prerequisite. So seven forms, not eight, plus one weaker thing of another kind.

CORRECTION 2: "forms 1 to 8 are not in its list" is overstated. Gap 112's handling points to the list in evidence/2026-11-13-package-3.1b/browser-required.md, "Every way a test could be left out". That list has the row "Retries, generated tests, test contexts", and its search (run-skip-scan.txt, section 4) looks for `ctx.`, `context.`, `.each(`, `.for(`, `.extend(` and `retry:`. So forms 7 and 8, the `.extend` half of 4, and the category of 2 were already on the hand-read list. Not recorded anywhere: 1 (no body), 3 (line break), 4 (import under another name), 5 (helper outside test/), 6 (written only on a condition), and the spelling of 2 (the hand search would not find `({ skip })`).

Narrower than it may read (run): with the plain word, forms 3 and 4 ARE found by the scan's second rule (`.skip(` on its own line; `check.skip(`), and a helper inside test/ is found.

WHY MINOR, NOT SERIOUS:
- Gap 112 (open) already states the principle ("the scan reads words") and exactly this risk ("A later change could leave a required check out in a way the scan does not read"). The finding adds entries to a recorded gap; it shows no new kind of failure.
- No instance at 839be17. I searched again: no file outside test/ names vitest; no other name for the API; no skip from a context; no test without a body; no line starting with one of the words; the only it.each (test/probe-phone.test.ts:120) and the six for-loops that write tests use fixed tables; the only test options are time limits.
- The outside review's item ("the required acceptance gate should fail when its prerequisites are missing") is enforced by behaviour, not by the word scan: test/acceptance-gate.test.ts:70-86 requires "7 failed (7)" and no "skipped" or "todo" from a child run. Read: forms 1 to 7 in acceptance-live.test.ts would each fail that. With Docker or the zip missing, that file fails `npm test` whatever another file does. test/preview-live.test.ts also fails without its prerequisites today (:165-167, :172).
- Who could use it: a later author of the builder's own tests, not the engine container or the generated app. A word scan cannot stop a deleted test or an emptied body either.

NOT BLOCKING: no hard rule is broken (no test is skipped; rule 8 is about an act of weakening, and none happened). The clause "no test in the suite can be skipped or marked to do" has been narrowed since 13 Nov by the options form in gap 112. That is already on record: docs/reviews/2026-11-14-state-of-merged-packages.md:15 ("one clause of its own wording is narrowed by gap 112"), and the package is still held at "built, not tested" (docs/STATUS.md:15, question 20). The first reviewer's note that the gap does not make that clause "tested" (build plan section 3, step 8) is fair for whoever re-marks 3.1b, but it is a point about gap 112 as a whole, not new with this finding.

WHAT TO DO: add forms 1, 3, 4 (import under another name), 5, 6 and the by-name spelling of 2 to gap 112 and to the hand-read list. The suggested run-time check (fail the run if any test ends skipped, to do, an expected failure or retried) is the real fix and would cover every file; gap 112 already calls such steps "further steps, not taken".

NOT LOOKED AT: the "first finding" this one refers to; the settings cases (G, H, I, K) in the first reviewer's probe; whether a reviewer did read each test added since 13 Nov against the list (the suite grew from 17 to 31 files).
